readme:
# WhatsApp Catch-Up

Your WhatsApp chats with customers, the way you know them from WhatsApp, with the
business part pulled out: who is waiting for an answer and for how long, the quotes and
appointments agreed in each chat, and what you promised.

Open the cabinet and your chats are there. Chats waiting for you are marked, and the
**Waiting for you** filter shows only those. Open one and a reply is already drafted
under it by Chat Keeper. Change it if you like, then press **Send**. Nothing is sent
until you press it.

## Getting started

1. Press **Connect WhatsApp** and scan the code with your phone, the way you would for
   WhatsApp Web.
2. Pick the chats this cabinet may read: your customers and suppliers. Only those are
   saved here, in **whatsapp**.
3. Choose **Reply after you say OK** so you can send from Cabinet.
4. Press **Catch me up now**, or wait for the morning: every day at 7:30 Chat Keeper
   reads what changed and drafts a reply for everyone waiting.

## Ideas to try

Press **Ideas** for things to ask once or to switch on every week, for example "List
every customer who asked for a quote", "Customers I haven't answered in 24 hours" and
"Build my customer list from my chats".

## Good to know

- WhatsApp doesn't officially support linking Cabinet this way, so keep it to your own
  chats. Lots of automatic messages can get a number blocked. Cabinet isn't responsible
  if that happens. Cabinet never sends on its own here: only your Send does.
- WhatsApp links to Cabinet on your computer. It can't be linked from Cabinet in the
  cloud.
- The people in the chats you pick are not told that Cabinet reads them.
- Tell Chat Keeper what matters and what to skip ("from now on, skip the family group"),
  and it keeps that in **whatsapp**, on the page called "What counts, and what to skip".

agents.name: Chat Keeper
agents.role: Reads the chats you picked and tells you which customers need you.

connectors.why: Reads the chats you pick and drafts replies you approve.
Puts plans from your chats on your calendar when you ask.

prompts.text: What appointments did I set this week?
Who hasn't heard back from me in a day?
List every customer who asked for a quote.
What did I promise customers this week?
Build my customer list from my chats.
Follow up on quotes with no answer. Show me the drafts first.
Did any customer complain this week?
Which customers haven't written in two months?
What did I agree with the plumber?
Find the address a customer sent me last month.
Who wrote to me from a number I haven't saved?
From now on, skip the family group.
Put the appointments from my chats on my calendar.
